    wayu configuration reference

    Everything wayu reads: wayu.toml (every table and key), what wayu manages for you (entries.json: PATH entries, aliases, constants; functions/, scripts/, completions/), the other files you may edit (hooks.conf, plugins.json, extra.<ext>, tools.<ext>, alias-sources.conf), where they live, and which files are generated.

    • Commands and flags: cli.md.
    • Behavior changes between versions: UPGRADING.md.

    <ext> below is the shell's extension: zsh, bash or fish.

    Directories#

    Variable Default Holds
    WAYU_CONFIG_DIR ~/.config/wayu Files you edit: wayu.toml, hooks.conf, alias-sources.conf, extra.<ext>, tools.<ext>, config.<ext>
    WAYU_DATA_DIR ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/wayu Data wayu manages: entries.json, plugins.json, functions/ (wayu function), scripts/ and bin/ (wayu script), and generated / runtime files: init.<ext>, core.<ext>, path_sync.<ext>, turbo.<ext>, plugins.<ext>, plugins/, completions/, backup/, .wayu.lock

    • Each variable is read independently: setting one never moves the other. wayu init creates both dirs; the first command that writes creates the data dir if it is missing.

    • wayu creates its dirs (and missing parents) 0700 whatever the umask, and wayu init removes group/other write from existing ones: they hold code your shell runs at startup, and bin/ is on PATH. wayu doctor reports a group/other-writable one as an error; wayu doctor --fix --yes tightens it.

    • WAYU_CONFIG_DIR and WAYU_DATA_DIR must be absolute paths: a relative one makes every command exit 78. A relative XDG_DATA_HOME is ignored (XDG spec), so the data dir is then ~/.local/share/wayu.

    • The rc line wayu init adds finds the data dir by itself:

      source "${WAYU_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/wayu}/init.zsh"

    • init.<ext> finds its files next to itself, so that line works without exporting either variable to the shell. If WAYU_CONFIG_DIR is unset, the config dir is ~/.config/wayu.

    • When either dir differs from the default, core.<ext> exports WAYU_CONFIG_DIR / WAYU_DATA_DIR, so wayu commands typed in that shell use the same dirs.

    • The [tools] evalcache lives outside both: ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/wayu/evalcache (wayu build clean deletes it).

    wayu.toml#

    $WAYU_CONFIG_DIR/wayu.toml is the file you edit for [shell], [settings], [tools] loaders and the native [prompt]. PATH entries, aliases and constants are not in it: wayu manages them in entries.json through wayu path|alias|const. wayu init creates this scaffold:

    [shell]
type = "zsh"

    After editing it by hand, run wayu build; changes apply to new shells. wayu toml validate checks the file (see Strict and lenient reading).

    Complete example#

    This file passes wayu toml validate and wayu build as-is.

    [shell]
type = "zsh"

[settings]
autosuggestions_accept_keys = [
  "^Y",
  "^[[121;5u",
]

[tools]
zoxide = { kind = "evalcache", args = "init zsh" }
atuin  = { args = "init zsh --disable-up-arrow", eager = true }
nvm    = { kind = "nvm" }
sdk    = { kind = "lazy", init_script = "~/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh", hook_commands = ["sdk"] }
keychain = { args = "--eval --quiet id_ed25519", login_only = true }

[prompt]
enabled = true
vi_mode = false
format  = "{username}{dir}{git_branch}[{language_context}](yellow){character} "

[prompt.username]
show_always = true
format = "[$user](white bold) in "

[prompt.dir]
format = "[$dir](cyan bold) "

[prompt.git_branch]
format = "on [$branch](magenta bold) "

[prompt.character]
success_symbol = "[>](green)"
error_symbol   = "[x](red)"

[prompt.contexts]
rust   = { format = "rs $version ", detect = ["Cargo.toml"] }
kotlin = { format = "kt ", detect = ["*.kt", "build.gradle.kts"] }

[prompt.interactive]
toggle_enabled = true
toggle_key = "^G"
vi_mode_indicator = true
async_rprompt = true
rprompt_format = "[ {git_pending}](242)"

    What it generates in core.zsh together with the entries.json example (excerpt):

    export GOBIN="${GOPATH}/bin"
export PAGER_OPTS="${LESS:--R}"
export PRICE="costs \$5"
_wayu_paths_apply <sig> ${HOME:+"${HOME}"'/.local/bin'} ${HOME:+"${HOME}"'/.cargo/bin'} ${GOPATH:+"${GOPATH}"'/bin'} '/opt/homebrew/bin'
_wayu_evalcache atuin init zsh --disable-up-arrow     # eager section
_wayu_evalcache zoxide init zsh                       # deferred section
if [[ -o login ]]; then
_wayu_evalcache keychain --eval --quiet id_ed25519
fi
alias onlead-logs='tail -f /var/log/onlead.log'

    TOML syntax wayu accepts#

    wayu uses one TOML 1.0 parser for every command (plus the TOML 1.1 conveniences \e, \xHH, and newlines / trailing commas in inline tables). A UTF-8 BOM, comments, dotted keys, quoted keys, multi-line arrays, floats and dates are all accepted.

    Arrays and inline tables are valid only where a key below says so: [settings] autosuggestions_accept_keys, [tools] entries and their hook_commands, and [prompt.contexts] entries.

    Keys:

    • A bare key may use A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. Anything else needs quotes: "my key" = .... Quoted keys are decoded everywhere ("q\"k" is the name q"k).
    • wayu writes wayu.toml only when it creates it (wayu init, or a command that needs a missing one); after that the file is yours.

    Strict and lenient reading#

    Reader On a syntax error
    wayu toml validate, wayu doctor, wayu backup restore (strict) Fail and name the line: Failed to parse <file>: line 5: invalid value "ls" (strings must be quoted)
    Everything else: the generator (wayu build, every write), the TUI (lenient) Use what was recovered; a line that is not valid TOML is skipped

    Strict-only failures: a key defined twice in one table, a table defined twice, an integer with leading zeros (007), an unquoted string, a raw control character inside a string (anything below 0x20 but tab, and DEL; multi-line strings may also hold line breaks: write the others as escapes such as \u001b), arrays or inline tables nested more than 128 deep.

    After parsing, wayu toml validate also checks:

    Check Error
    Top-level version, if present, is "1.0" Unsupported config version: 2.0
    [shell] type (case-insensitive) is zsh, bash or fish Invalid shell: unknown (must be zsh, bash, or fish)
    No [paths], [aliases] or [env] (in any form): those entries live in entries.json Validation failed: line 4: [env] is not read from wayu.toml: its entries are managed with 'wayu const add' (stored in <data>/entries.json); move them there and delete the table
    shell, settings, tools, prompt are tables ([tools], not [[tools]] or tools = ...) Validation failed: line 1: [[tools]]: tools must be a table ([tools]), not an array of tables

    Keys and tables wayu does not read are warnings, not errors (see Keys wayu does not read).

    It does not check [tools] args (wayu build does) or [prompt]. Exit status: 0 valid, 65 invalid, 78 before wayu init.

    [shell]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    type string "zsh" zsh, bash or fish (case-insensitive). Written lowercase by wayu init and any command that creates a missing wayu.toml.

    type is a record of the shell the config was set up for and is checked by toml validate; it does not choose the shell. wayu acts for the shell named by --shell, else $SHELL, and regenerates the files of every other shell already initialized in the data dir (init.<ext> or core.<ext> exists). A top-level shell = "..." string is not read (toml validate rejects it).

    [settings]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    autosuggest boolean false zsh only (interactive). Built-in fish-like suggestions from history, in place of the zsh-autosuggestions plugin: see Autosuggestions. A non-boolean value is an error (toml validate, doctor).
    autosuggest_style string "fg=8" zsh only. How the suggestion is drawn: a region_highlight spec (fg=244, fg=8,underline; one line, at most 64 bytes, else an error).
    autosuggestions_accept_keys array of strings ["^Y", "^[[121;5u"] zsh only. Key sequences that accept the whole suggestion: bound to autosuggest-accept (zsh-autosuggestions) in the main, emacs and viins keymaps, or, with autosuggest = true, to wayu-suggest-accept in emacs and viins. Entries must start with ^ or contain [; others, non-strings, empties and duplicates are ignored. An empty or missing array uses the default. The array may span lines.
    auto_optimize boolean false When an open shell notices that a startup file changed (prompt hook) and it has lines wayu optimize can move, move them right away (backups first) and print what moved, instead of printing the wayu: ~/.zshrc changed: N lines can be optimized notice.

    | compinit_guard | boolean | true | zsh only. After wayu's compinit, compinit is a function that only registers the completions (#compdef / #autoload files) of fpath dirs added since; its flags (-C, -i, -u, -d <dump>, ...) are accepted and ignored. An installer's autoload -Uz compinit && compinit in .zshrc then costs a glob of the new dirs instead of a second full completion setup (audit, dump check/rewrite), and its dirs' completions work even with -C. The same registration runs once at the first prompt, for dirs added to fpath without a compinit call. false: later compinit calls are zsh's own. | | defer_plugins | boolean | false | zsh only. Load the plugins (plugins.zsh, plugins/config.zsh) after the first prompt is drawn (through zsh-defer) instead of during startup. They then load after tools.zsh / extra.zsh: code there that needs a plugin widget should run through zsh-defer. | | highlight | boolean | false | zsh only (interactive). Built-in syntax highlighting of the command line, in place of the zsh-syntax-highlighting / fast-syntax-highlighting plugins: see Syntax highlighting. A non-boolean value is an error. | | highlight_styles | table of strings | see styles | zsh only. Per-style region_highlight specs, as an inline table (highlight_styles = { command = "fg=blue", comment = "fg=244" }) or a [settings.highlight_styles] table. "none": not highlighted. A value that isn't a one-line string of at most 64 bytes is an error; an unknown style name is a warning (ignored). | | lazy_compinit | boolean | false | zsh only. No compinit at startup: the completion widgets (Tab, ^D list, ...) set up completion on first use and then complete. compdef calls made before that are queued and replayed. $_comps and completion functions don't exist until then. |

    The plugin bindings are written to <data>/plugins/config.zsh, which core.zsh sources after the plugins; they apply only when the autosuggest-accept widget exists. No other [settings] key is read.

    Autosuggestions#

    autosuggest = true puts suggestions in core.zsh itself (interactive zsh; nothing forks, no extra files). As you type, the newest history entry that starts with the line (typed glob characters are literal) is shown after the cursor in autosuggest_style. It is computed in a zle-line-pre-redraw hook (add-zle-hook-widget, which zsh-syntax-highlighting 0.8+ also uses) instead of wrapping every widget at the first prompt and before every prompt as the zsh-autosuggestions plugin does.

    • Accept all: forward-char, end-of-line, vi-forward-char, vi-end-of-line, vi-add-eol (→, ^F, ^E/End where bound, vi l $ A) with the cursor at the end of the line, and the autosuggestions_accept_keys (default ^Y).
    • Accept part: forward-word, emacs-forward-word, vi-forward-word, vi-forward-word-end, vi-forward-blank-word, vi-forward-blank-word-end, vi-find-next-char, vi-find-next-char-skip (M-f, vi w e W E f t) move through the suggestion and take what ends up before the cursor.
    • Only these 13 widgets are wrapped (chaining to what was bound before); the suggestion is gone when the cursor isn't at the end, after history and search widgets (the line already came from history) and once the line is accepted: Enter runs only what you typed.
    • With autosuggest = true the zsh-autosuggestions plugin is not loaded, even if installed and enabled (wayu doctor warns until it is removed or disabled). defer_plugins / lazy_compinit don't affect it (it is set up at startup; it is cheap). bash and fish ignore it (doctor notes it).
    • Suggestions come from history (most recent match); a multi-line history entry is suggested whole. When nothing in history matches and the line is a single word, the shortest command name on PATH starting with it is suggested (ties: alphabetical), e.g. no → node if no no… command is shorter. No completion strategy beyond that.

    Syntax highlighting#

    highlight = true puts a syntax highlighter in core.zsh itself (interactive zsh; nothing forks, no extra files, no widget is wrapped). It runs in a zle-line-pre-redraw hook, like the autosuggestions: zsh's own lexer (${(z)BUFFER}) splits the line into words, which are colored by region_highlight entries (tagged memo=wayu-highlight on zsh 5.9+; other entries, such as the suggestion's or your own, are kept). The line is only looked at again when it changed, and an edit anywhere in it re-highlights from the word before the change until the words after it are back in the state they had (usually a word or two), not the whole line. Lines already entered at a continuation prompt (PS2) are highlighted with the current one, so its words keep their meaning. Command lookups and path checks are cached until a command runs or the directory / PATH changes.

    The style names are zsh-syntax-highlighting's (its ZSH_HIGHLIGHT_STYLES values carry over) and so are the defaults:

    Style Default What
    unknown-token fg=red,bold a command that doesn't exist (yet)
    reserved-word fg=yellow if then for do case in always [[ ]] { } (( )) ( ) !, case pattern parentheses ...
    alias fg=green an alias
    suffix-alias fg=green,underline a file run through a suffix alias (alias -s)
    global-alias fg=cyan a global alias (alias -g), anywhere on the line
    builtin fg=green a builtin (typeset & co. too)
    function fg=green a function
    command fg=green a command on PATH, or an executable path
    precommand fg=green,underline sudo doas env command builtin exec noglob nocorrect time nohup nice -: the next word is a command again (after their options; sudo -u user, env -u NAME, env NAME=value are understood)
    commandseparator none ; && || | |& & ;;, newline
    autodirectory fg=green,underline a directory in command position, with setopt autocd
    path underline an existing file or directory (~ and ~name expanded)
    path_prefix underline the last word, while it is the start of an existing name
    globbing fg=blue a word with unquoted * ? [...]
    expansion fg=cyan $var ${...} $((...)) outside double quotes (wayu's; zsh-syntax-highlighting leaves them plain)
    command-substitution-delimiter fg=magenta $( and ); the inside is highlighted as a command line
    process-substitution-delimiter fg=magenta <( >( =( and )
    back-quoted-argument-delimiter fg=magenta the backticks of `...`
    single-hyphen-option none -x
    double-hyphen-option none --long
    single-quoted-argument fg=yellow '...' (to the end while unterminated)
    double-quoted-argument fg=yellow "..." (to the end while unterminated)
    dollar-quoted-argument fg=yellow $'...'
    dollar-double-quoted-argument fg=cyan $var ${...} $((...)) inside "..."
    back-double-quoted-argument fg=cyan \" \$ \` \\ inside "..."
    back-dollar-quoted-argument fg=cyan \n & co. inside $'...'
    assign none NAME=value before a command or after typeset & co. (the value is highlighted too), name=( ... )
    redirection fg=yellow > >> < 2> &> <<< >& {fd}> ...
    comment fg=black,bold # ..., with setopt interactive_comments
    history-expansion fg=blue !! !$ !-2 !str ... (with banghist; also inside "...", where zsh expands them too)
    named-fd none {fd} in {fd}>file
    numeric-fd none the descriptor after >& / <& (2>&1, >&-)
    bracket-level-1 fg=blue,bold ( ) [ ] { } outside quotes, by nesting depth (levels 1–3, then 1 again)
    bracket-level-2 fg=green,bold
    bracket-level-3 fg=magenta,bold
    bracket-error fg=red,bold a bracket without its pair (or closed by the wrong one)
    cursor-matchingbracket standout the pair of the bracket under the cursor
    • Heredoc bodies are skipped; what follows the delimiter line is a command line again.
    • The selected region, the incremental search match and pasted text keep their zle_highlight look (default: standout / underline / standout).
    • With highlight = true the zsh-syntax-highlighting and fast-syntax-highlighting plugins are not loaded, even if installed and enabled (wayu doctor warns until they are removed or disabled). defer_plugins / lazy_compinit don't affect it (it is set up at startup; it is cheap). bash and fish ignore it (doctor notes it).
    • Brackets: (( )) of arithmetic, [[ ]], [ ] as words, the parentheses of case patterns and of name=(...) are syntax, not brackets; brackets inside "..." are not counted.
    • After noglob, * ? [...] are not highlighted as globs; after command -v, the name is highlighted as a command.
    • Not covered (zsh-syntax-highlighting's other highlighters and some main ones): rc-quote, hashed-command, path separators; a line longer than 20000 characters is not highlighted. tests/highlight_diff compares the highlighter with fast-syntax-highlighting and lists the intended differences.

    Interactive-only parts of core.zsh (completion, the native prompt, plugins, zsh-defer) are skipped in non-interactive zsh (zsh -c, scripts): there it sets constants, secrets, PATH entries, functions/, config.zsh, [tools], tools.zsh, extra.zsh and aliases (zsh expands aliases in zsh -c too), and zsh-defer is a no-op. Sourcing init.zsh again in a shell (e.g. from both .zshenv and .zshrc) doesn't reorder PATH, add wayu's completions dir to fpath twice, source an already loaded plugin again or redo compinit.

    [tools]#

    Shell integrations for installed tools, generated into core.<ext>:

    [tools]
zoxide   = { kind = "evalcache", args = "init zsh" }
atuin    = { args = "init zsh --disable-up-arrow", eager = true }
nvm      = { kind = "nvm" }
conda    = { kind = "conda" }
sdk      = { kind = "lazy", init_script = "~/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh", hook_commands = ["sdk"] }
keychain = { args = "--eval --quiet id_ed25519", login_only = true }

[tools.direnv]          # a sub-table works too
args = "hook zsh"

    Each entry is an inline table or a [tools.<name>] sub-table; other values are ignored. Entries are emitted in file order (an entry may rely on one above it).

    Key Type Default Meaning
    kind string "evalcache" evalcache, nvm, conda or lazy. Any other kind is skipped with a # wayu: unknown kind comment.
    args string "" evalcache: arguments for the tool, e.g. "init zsh" (rules below).
    eager boolean false evalcache only: load before the prompt and plugins (tools that bind keys, e.g. atuin). Ignored for other kinds.
    login_only boolean false Load only in login shells ([[ -o login ]], shopt -q login_shell, status is-login). Wins over eager.
    init_script string lazy: script sourced on first use (leading ~ and $VAR expand; sourced only when non-empty).
    hook_commands array of strings lazy: commands that trigger the load.

    Booleans must be TOML booleans: eager = "true" is ignored.

    Kinds:

    Kind What it generates
    evalcache Runs command <name> <args> (the table key is the binary, looked up in PATH only, never a function or alias), caches the output in ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/wayu/evalcache and sources the cache. The cache is rebuilt when the binary changes (zsh: resolved path, size, mtime, inode; bash: path, mtime, inode/target; fish: path, mtime, needs fish 3.5+, else uncached). A tool that is not installed is skipped silently. Run wayu build clean when the init output depends on config or the environment. The tool name must be a valid alias name.
    nvm Lazy NVM: needs $NVM_DIR (default ~/.nvm) to exist. Puts the default node on PATH at once; nvm.sh is sourced on the first nvm call. zsh also wraps node, npm, npx, corepack and switches versions on cd into a dir with .nvmrc / .node-version. No fish version (skipped with a comment).
    conda Lazy conda: finds the first of ~/anaconda3, ~/miniconda3, ~/miniforge3, /opt/homebrew/anaconda3, /opt/anaconda3; conda and mamba load it on first call. No fish version (skipped).
    lazy Defines each hook_commands entry as a wrapper that sources init_script once, then runs the real command. Needs both keys (else skipped with a comment); entries that are not valid alias names are skipped. In fish, init_script must end in .fish.

    args rules. args is split into words the way the shell does (single and double quotes, backslashes) and each word is re-quoted in the generated call, so it can never run code at startup:

    • Expand: $NAME / ${NAME...} (same rules as constants) outside single quotes, and a leading ~ / ~/.
    • Literal: everything else, including {a,b} (no brace expansion).
    • Refused: a newline, ; & | < > ( ), $(...), backticks, unquoted glob characters * ? [, and a word that mixes quoted and unquoted $. wayu build exits 78 naming the tool (ERROR: wayu.toml [tools] foo: args contains the shell operator ";"); other regenerations skip the tool with a warning on stderr.

    For example args = 'init "$HOME/x y" ~/z {a,b}' generates _wayu_evalcache foo init "${HOME}/x y" "${HOME}/z" '{a,b}'.

    Shell name in args. One entry serves every shell: a word zsh or bash in args becomes the shell whose file is generated, and --zsh / --bash becomes --<shell>. args = "init zsh" runs zoxide init zsh in core.zsh, zoxide init bash in core.bash and zoxide init fish in fish ([tools] load in fish too).

    Where they load (see Load order): eager evalcache tools before the prompt and plugins; all other non-login tools ("deferred") after the plugins; login_only tools after tools.<ext> and extra.<ext>. "Deferred" is a position in the file, not a key, and not zsh-defer.

    [prompt]#

    A native prompt for zsh and fish, off by default. It is generated only when [prompt] enabled = true, and set up only in interactive shells. bash ignores the whole table. fish differences: see fish.

    The [prompt] tables are read with the same TOML parser as the rest of wayu.toml: comments, dotted keys, [prompt.contexts.<name>] tables and multi-line strings work, and a value of the wrong type keeps the default.

    [prompt]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    enabled boolean false Generate the prompt. Without it wayu leaves PROMPT, keymaps and zle widgets alone.
    vi_mode boolean false bindkey -v, KEYTIMEOUT=1 (not exported), and the mode indicator unless [prompt.interactive] vi_mode_indicator = false. Without it the keymap is left alone and {character} shows success/error by exit status.
    format string "{username}{dir}{git_branch}{character} " Prompt layout. \n starts a new line.

    format tokens (unknown tokens produce nothing; other text is literal):

    Token Shows
    {username} [prompt.username] format
    {hostname} [prompt.hostname] format
    {localip} [prompt.localip] format
    {dir} [prompt.dir] format
    {git_branch} [prompt.git_branch] format, only inside a git work tree
    {character} The prompt symbol (see [prompt.character])
    {language_context} / {context_icon} The [prompt.contexts] format of the detected project type; the shell name when none matches

    A token may be styled as [{token}](style). Plain text in format is not styled ([text](style) is literal there); use module formats for that.

    Styles (used in [text](style) and [{token}](style)): space-separated words bold, italic, underline, dim, a color name (black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, orange, pink, purple, gray/grey, lime, teal) or a 256-color number (242). Unknown words are ignored.

    Module formats use the [text](style) syntax plus the module's variables. Config text is always literal: $(...) in it never runs.

    [prompt.username]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    format string "[$user](white bold) in " $user = the user name.
    show_always boolean false Show the user name everywhere. Default: only over SSH or as root.

    [prompt.hostname]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    format string "$hostname" $hostname = short host name.

    [prompt.localip]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    format string "$localip" $localip = IPv4 address (ipconfig getifaddr en0, else ip -4 route get 1), computed at every prompt.

    [prompt.dir]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    format string "[$dir](cyan bold) " $dir = current dir with ~, $pwd = full path, $basename = last component.

    [prompt.git_branch]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    format string "on [$branch](magenta bold) " $branch = branch name, or the first 7 characters of the commit when detached. Read from .git/HEAD without running git (worktrees, submodules and $GIT_DIR included).

    [prompt.character]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    success_symbol string ➜ Symbol after a successful command (and in vi insert mode).
    error_symbol string ✗ Symbol after a failed command.
    vimcmd_symbol string ❮ vi normal mode.
    vimcmd_visual_symbol string ❮ vi visual mode.
    vimcmd_replace_symbol string ❮ vi replace mode: R, and r while it waits for the character.

    Only the text between [ and ] is used ("[>](green)" gives >); the style part is ignored. Colors are fixed: green on success, red on error; in vi mode orange (202) insert, green normal, purple (129) visual/replace.

    [prompt.contexts]#

    [prompt.contexts]
rust   = { format = "rs $version ", detect = ["Cargo.toml"] }
kotlin = { format = "kt ", detect = ["*.kt", "build.gradle.kts"] }

    One line per project type: name = { format = "...", detect = [...] }.

    Field Meaning
    format What {language_context} shows. $version = the tool version, fetched in the background (needs async_rprompt); only the built-in names rust, bun, dart, ruby, elixir, odin, golang, deno, nodejs, python, zig have a version command.
    detect File names or globs (*, ?) checked in the current directory on cd. The first entry (in file order) with a match wins. Entries with characters other than letters, digits, . _ - / + @ * ? or non-ASCII are ignored.

    User entries are tested before the built-in detectors (rust, bun, gleam, swift, dart, php, ruby, elixir, erlang, haskell, julia, odin, golang, nim, ocaml, nix, deno, elm, crystal, perl, buf, nodejs, java, scala, python, zig, rlang, lua, docker, aws). A user entry replaces the built-in one of the same name. A built-in match without a user format shows the shell name.

    [prompt.interactive]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    toggle_enabled boolean false Bind toggle_key to switch between the full and the minimal prompt. Bound in viins + vicmd with vi_mode, else in emacs.
    toggle_key string "^P" Key sequence for the toggle.
    transient_enabled boolean true Minimal prompt = current dir + success/error symbol. false: minimal prompt = %~ ➜ . Only reachable through the toggle.
    vi_mode_indicator boolean true With vi_mode, track the keymap in {character}. zle-line-init / zle-keymap-select already defined are kept and run first.
    context_aware boolean true Detect the project type on cd (for {language_context}).
    async_rprompt boolean true Background job after each command: git changed-file count (right prompt) and context version. Started only in a git work tree or a context with a version command; elsewhere the right prompt is cleared without forking.
    rprompt_format string "[ {git_pending}](242)" Right prompt, shown when the work tree has changes. {git_pending} = number of changed files, {git_branch} = branch.

    Prompt in fish#

    core.fish defines fish_prompt (and fish_right_prompt with async_rprompt) from the same tables, in interactive shells, before the plugins: a plugin or config.fish code that defines fish_prompt later wins. Same tokens, module variables, styles (as ANSI colors; a styled part ends with a full reset), symbols and colors. A render runs only fish builtins, except {localip}. Differences:

    • vi_mode = true sets fish_key_bindings to fish_vi_key_bindings; {character} follows $fish_bind_mode (insert, default = normal, visual, replace / replace_one) and fish_mode_prompt is emptied. Without vi_mode the key bindings and fish_mode_prompt are left alone.
    • toggle_key must be ^X (a letter, bound as \cx); it is bound from fish_user_key_bindings, which calls one defined before wayu first. Other keys are not bound (a comment in core.fish says so).
    • [prompt.contexts] detection runs on $PWD changes; a glob matches with * only.
    • async_rprompt starts fish --no-config in the background per prompt (only in a git work tree or a versioned context) and repaints on SIGUSR1.

    [scripts]#

    Key Type Default Meaning
    default_lang string "swift" Language of wayu script new without --lang: swift, python, ruby, node, bun, bash, zsh, fish, perl, lua or sh. Another value is an error for toml validate (exit 65), doctor and script new (exit 78). 
    [scripts]
default_lang = "python"

    [secrets]#

    [secrets]
backend = "auto"

    Encrypted constants (wayu const add NAME [VALUE] --secret) are kept in <data>/secrets.json (0600, managed by wayu, not for hand edits):

    {"version": 1, "cipher": "chacha20poly1305", "values": {"NAME": "<base64 nonce||ciphertext||tag>"}, "run_only": ["NAME"]}

    Each value is encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305 under a 256-bit master key, with a random nonce and the variable name as associated data. In entries.json a secret is {"name": "NAME", "secret": true}, with no value, at its place in the constants' order. A run-only secret (--run-only) is also listed in run_only (written only when non-empty) and marked "run_only": true in entries.json; it is never written to the session cache, so shells never export it, and only wayu secrets run decrypts it. The mark is part of the associated data (NAME + \0run-only), so removing it from secrets.json makes the value fail to decrypt rather than get exported. The file is read strictly: any other field, text after the object, a name that is not a shell variable name, a non-string value, or a run_only name missing from values makes it malformed (secret commands exit 78, doctor reports an error). backend says where the master key lives:

    backend Key storage
    "auto" (default) keychain on macOS; secret-service on Linux when secret-tool is installed in /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /bin or /run/current-system/sw/bin; else file
    "keychain" macOS login keychain: generic password, service wayu-master-key, account wayu-<id>, via /usr/bin/security. Storing (first secret, rekey) runs security -i and writes the command on its stdin: the key is never on a command line.
    "secret-service" freedesktop Secret Service via secret-tool (service wayu account wayu-<id>) from one of those dirs; the key goes over stdin
    "file" <config>/secret.key: 64 hex characters, 0600, created exclusively; refused when group/other can read it. Protects against reading the data dir alone, not against reading your whole home. It lives in the config dir: never commit it to a dotfiles repo (add secret.key to its .gitignore); anyone with the file and secrets.json can decrypt every secret.

    security and secret-tool are never looked up in PATH: a program of that name planted earlier in PATH would receive the key.

    <id> is 16 hex digits identifying the data dir (FNV-1a 64 of its path, the same id as in the session cache name): each data dir (another WAYU_DATA_DIR, a test HOME) has its own key and never reads another's. wayu doctor prints the account (keychain (account wayu-…)). A key left by wayu 6.0 (one shared item: keychain account wayu, Secret Service account master) is copied to the per-data-dir account the first time it is needed, when it decrypts the data dir's secrets.json; the old item is kept.

    Any other value is an error (toml validate exits 65; secret commands exit 78). The key is created with the first secret; wayu never creates a new key while secrets.json holds values (it would make them undecryptable). wayu secrets rekey replaces it and re-encrypts everything: the new store is written to secrets.json.rekey first, then the key is saved, then the file is renamed over secrets.json; if wayu is interrupted in between, the next command that reads the store finishes or undoes the rekey, whichever matches the stored key.

    At shell start core.<ext> sources the session cache ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-<data>/run}}/wayu-<uid>/secrets-<id>.<ext> (single-quoted export / set -gx lines, 0600 in a 0700 dir you own) when it is newer than secrets.json, without forking in zsh (bash and fish run one ls -ldn to read the dir's mode). The dir must be yours, not a symlink and without group/other permission bits (else <data>/run/wayu-<uid> is used), and the file must be yours and not a symlink; with neither XDG_RUNTIME_DIR nor TMPDIR set the cache lives under <data>/run (0700), never in a shared /tmp. Otherwise it runs wayu secrets cache once to (re)write it. If the key is unavailable or a value does not decrypt, one wayu: secrets not loaded: … line goes to stderr and startup continues without the secrets. The cache holds the values in plaintext on disk until it is deleted: every change to secrets.json deletes it, and wayu secrets lock deletes it by hand. Both remove the caches of this data dir from every cache dir wayu wrote one to (each is recorded in <data>/run/cache-dirs), whatever TMPDIR / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR the deleting command runs with. Secret values are literal: no $VAR or ~ expansion.

    Decrypted values are never written to core.<ext>, path_sync.<ext>, turbo.<ext>, backups or logs; only to the session cache and to the output of wayu const get NAME (and to the environment of wayu secrets run's command). wayu doctor checks the backend, the key, the store's mode, that every secret decrypts, and the cache dir.

    Multi-machine secrets (experimental)#

    Experimental: the commands and the version 2 format below may change in a minor release; a format change still migrates automatically. Version 1 stays valid: a store becomes version 2 only when you run wayu secrets recipient add (or recovery add), which backs up the version 1 file, writes version 2, verifies it and prints a one-time notice (wayu 7.0 cannot read version 2: upgrade every machine that syncs the file first). wayu 7.0 reading a newer version exits 78 naming the upgrade.

    {
  "version": 2,
  "cipher": "chacha20poly1305",
  "key_id": "3f9a1c0e5b7d2a41",
  "recipients": [
    {"name": "laptop", "recipient": "age1…", "stanza": "<share> <body>"}
  ],
  "recovery": {"recipient": "age1…", "stanza": "…", "kdf": "argon2id", "m": 65536, "t": 3, "p": 4, "salt": "…", "identity": "…"},
  "rotations": [
    {"from": "a17c…", "to": "3f9a1c0e5b7d2a41", "proof": "…"}
  ],
  "values": {"NAME": "<base64 nonce||ciphertext||tag>"},
  "run_only": ["NAME"]
}
    • values / run_only: exactly as in version 1 (same key, AAD and lines; a migrated store's data key is its 7.0 master key).
    • key_id: the data key's fingerprint, the first 8 bytes of HKDF-SHA256(key, info wayu/secrets/key-id) in lower-case hex.
    • recipients (at least one, sorted by name): name is 1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, unique; recipient an age X25519 recipient (bech32 age1…, unique; age1pq1… is reserved and refused); stanza the data key wrapped as in age's X25519 recipient type (HKDF-SHA256 with salt = share ‖ recipient and info age-encryption.org/v1/X25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a zero nonce): unpadded base64 of the 32-byte ephemeral share and the 48-byte body. The ephemeral key is derived from the data key, the name and the recipient, so wayu can recompute every stanza: one it did not write (an added or renamed entry) is refused before the key is wrapped to it again (78, naming recipient rm).
    • rotations (at most 16, oldest dropped): each new data key's verification key and an Ed25519 signature by the previous data key (both derived from the keys). A machine that cached an older key accepts the new one only through this chain, and not when it lists a machine this one saw removed. The proof does not reveal the new key to holders of the old one, but a removed machine that can still write the synced file can sign a key of its own from the old key: a machine that has not synced since the recipient rm accepts it (it prints the recipient changes) and stays exposed until it syncs the real file. After recipient rm, rotate the real credentials upstream.
    • recovery (optional, wayu-only): a random X25519 identity sealed with ChaCha20-Poly1305 under argon2id(passphrase, salt; m KiB, t passes, p lanes, bounded to 1 GiB / 16 / 16), and the data key wrapped to it. salt and the parameters are not authenticated: recovery unlock uses only the parameters wayu writes (m 65536, t 3, p 4) and refuses others (78); a changed salt fails like a wrong passphrase. The recovery passphrase is not machine-bound: recipient rm does not change it, so replace it (recovery rm --yes, recovery add) when the removed machine knew it.
    • Strict like version 1: unknown fields (at any level), duplicate keys, names or recipients, a bad key_id, an empty recipient list or more than 16 rotations make the file malformed (78).

    What each machine verified is kept after the cached key in its master-key item (the backend's item, or secret.key), never in secrets.json: ;v=2;r=NAME:age1…,…;x=NAME:age1…,…;s=KEYID,… — it has read version 2, the recipients it last verified, the ones it saw removed and the data keys it replaced (32 kept). From then on a version 1 secrets.json (a downgrade) and a store under a replaced key (a rollback) are errors (78) naming the fix, and wayu 7.0 cannot read that item (it reads only the key of a one-machine item, which has no state). Not detected: an older copy of individual values under the same data key (a value rolled back by a synced older file), and anything on a machine before it first adopts a key.

    This machine's identity (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…) is kept by the backend: keychain / Secret Service account wayu-<id>-identity (same service as the master key); file: <config>/identity.key, in age's identity-file layout (# public key: age1…), 0600, created exclusively, never replaced. Like secret.key, never commit it (wayu doctor warns when either sits in a git work tree without being ignored). The verified data key stays in the master key's item. wayu doctor also checks that this machine is a listed recipient whose stanza unwraps, that the cached key is the store's (or a proven rotation of it), that every value decrypts with it (a concurrent rekey on two machines leaves values under the losing key: doctor names them), that every stanza is wayu's, and warns about sync-conflict copies next to the store (secrets.sync-conflict-*.json, secrets 2.json).

    The session cache is sourced while it is newer than secrets.json (a -nt test, no fork). Every wayu write deletes it, but a secrets.json replaced by a sync tool that keeps an older mtime (e.g. rsync -t) is not noticed: the shell keeps the cached values until the next wayu write, wayu secrets lock, or wayu secrets cache (which always rewrites it).

    wayu backup restore entries over a version 2 store keeps its recipients: the backup's secrets.json values are restored under the current header when they decrypt with the current data key (else the restore is refused).

    Keys wayu does not read#

    wayu reads only the keys and tables listed above. Anything else (for example wayu_version, [settings] auto_backup, [path], [[plugins]] — plugins live in plugins.json —, [profile.*], [constants]) has no effect: wayu toml validate prints a warning per unknown key or table, with its line (⚠ line 5: unknown key settings.auto_backup (ignored)), and still exits 0; wayu doctor reports them as a warning. Keys inside an unknown table are not listed one by one.

    Managed data#

    PATH entries, aliases and constants are data wayu manages: wayu path|alias| const add|rm, the TUI and templates edit them, and wayu build compiles them into core.<ext>. They are not read from wayu.toml; a [paths], [aliases] or [env] table there is an error for wayu toml validate and wayu doctor, naming the command to use instead.

    entries.json#

    $WAYU_DATA_DIR/entries.json:

    {
  "version": 1,
  "paths": [
    {"key": "local_bin", "dir": "~/.local/bin"},
    {"key": "cargo_bin", "dir": "$HOME/.cargo/bin"},
    {"key": "go_bin", "dir": "$GOPATH/bin"},
    {"key": "homebrew_bin", "dir": "/opt/homebrew/bin"}
  ],
  "aliases": [
    {"name": "ll", "value": "ls -lah"},
    {"name": "gs", "value": "git status"},
    {"name": "onlead-logs", "value": "tail -f /var/log/onlead.log"},
    {"name": "gl", "value": "git log --format=\"%h %s\""}
  ],
  "env": [
    {"name": "EDITOR", "value": "nvim"},
    {"name": "GOPATH", "value": "$HOME/go"},
    {"name": "GOBIN", "value": "${GOPATH}/bin"},
    {"name": "PAGER_OPTS", "value": "${LESS:--R}"},
    {"name": "PRICE", "value": "costs $5"},
    {"name": "GITHUB_TOKEN", "value": "ghp_example"}
  ]
}
    Field Meaning
    version The number 1 (required). Any other value, "1" or 1.0 is an error.
    paths[] {"key", "dir"}: PATH entries, highest priority first. key: letters, digits, _; dir: non-empty, no : or newline.
    aliases[] {"name", "value"}: aliases. name follows the alias name rule; value must not be blank.
    env[] {"name", "value"}: constants (exported variables), in export order. name: letters, digits, _, not starting with a digit. An encrypted one is {"name", "secret": true} (no value), optionally "run_only": true.
    fpath[] Strings, zsh only: completion dirs put on fpath (first = front) before wayu's compinit; the dump is rebuilt when their file list changes. Same expansion as PATH entries. No :, newline or glob character (`* ? [ ] ( ) < >
    generators[] {"shell", "cmd", "args"}: source <(cmd args) / eval "$(cmd args)" lines moved by wayu optimize. core.<shell> (only that shell's) runs _wayu_evalcache cmd args after everything else, before the aliases; zsh/bash in interactive shells only. args follows the [tools] args rules. Written only when non-empty.
    • Writes are atomic (temp file + rename, symlinks kept), under the lock shared by concurrent wayu commands, owner-only (0600), pretty-printed with one entry per line, in stable order: a write changes only the entries it touches. Each write is backed up first (wayu backup restore entries).
    • Reading is strict. A missing file is an empty store. Anything else must be exactly one JSON document (nothing after it, no trailing commas, no key twice in an object, valid UTF-8, no NUL character) that fits the table above: every field with its type, no unknown field, required fields present, names valid, the same key / name at most once per section. Otherwise every command that reads it exits 78, naming the file and the problem; nothing is written. wayu doctor reports it too.
    • It is safe to edit by hand while no wayu command runs; run wayu build afterwards (open shells also notice a newer file, see PATH entries).

    PATH entries#

    wayu path add ~/.local/bin --portable stores $HOME/.local/bin for use across machines. This opt-in only applies inside HOME; the default still resolves and stores an absolute directory. The file format is unchanged.

    wayu path add ~/.local/bin, wayu path add go_bin='$GOPATH/bin': each entry is a key (a label) and a dir.

    • Order is priority. Entries go to the front of PATH in store order (the first entry wins). wayu path add appends; existing entries never move.

    • Keys are labels. The shell never sees them; wayu path rm <key> and wayu path add name=dir use them. path add derives one when not given: lowercase, non-alphanumerics to _, .local to hidden_local, a generic basename (bin, ...) prefixed with its parent (/usr/local/bin to local_bin), _2, _3 on collision.

    • Expansion happens in the shell, at startup and at each re-sync: a leading ~ or ~/ becomes $HOME; $NAME and ${NAME} expand (an constant is already exported because constants come first). Nothing else expands: ${X:-y}, $(...), a bare $ stay literal. An entry whose variable is unset or empty is dropped (never turned into /bin).

    • Skipped at runtime: directories that do not exist (re-checked when the list is re-applied), values containing : or a newline (warning on stderr), empty values, and repeats of an earlier value.

    • Relative paths (./node_modules/.bin) are kept as written: the shell tests them against its current directory when the list is applied and, once on PATH, resolves them against the current directory at every command lookup. wayu doctor counts them with the entries it leaves alone, never as missing. wayu path add itself never stores a relative path: it resolves ~, $VAR and relative arguments to an absolute directory, which must exist (and be a directory).

    • Integration with PATH: wayu removes only directories it put on PATH itself (tracked in _WAYU_PATHS_MANAGED); a system directory that is also a PATH entry is moved to wayu's position but never removed. In zsh the session also gets typeset -U path. In fish the dirs move to the front in store order, like fish_add_path -gpm.

    • Open shells pick up PATH changes at their next prompt: the prompt hook re-applies path_sync.<ext> when its signature changes, and runs wayu build first when wayu.toml or entries.json is newer than it. That build never compiles: stale scripts are built by a background wayu script build. When that build fails (e.g. a malformed entries.json save), the hook writes path_sync.<ext>.regen-failed and tries again after the next save of either file.

    Aliases#

    wayu alias add ll 'ls -lah': each entry is a name and a command (value).

    One rule for alias add, the TUI, templates and entries.json:

    Rule
    Name characters Printable ASCII except whitespace, quotes, ` $ \ = / ^ ; & | < > ( ) { } [ ] * ? # ~ !; not starting with -. .., g.st, 1x, k8s-ctx are fine
    Reserved names Names starting with _wayu (wayu's helpers), . and if then else elif fi case esac for while until do done in function time select coproc declare typeset local export readonly unset return exit cd pwd echo test true false are refused
    Length At most 255 characters
    Command Must not be blank; no NUL byte, valid UTF-8

    Generated code: zsh/bash alias name='command'; fish a function function name --wraps 'command' --description 'alias name command' whose body is eval 'command' (string escape -- $argv) (what fish's alias defines, but the command is never parsed as code when the function is defined; arguments pass through literally). The command is single-quoted and stored verbatim, so $VAR in it expands when the alias runs. Aliases are emitted sorted by name, last in core.<ext> (after plugins and tools), so an alias never breaks a function wayu or a plugin defines.

    Constants#

    wayu const add GOPATH '$HOME/go': each entry is a name and a value, exported as export NAME="..." (zsh/bash) or set -gx NAME "..." (fish), in store order, so a later value can use an earlier one.

    Names: an ASCII letter or _, then letters, digits or _ (no -), not a reserved word (list above), at most 255 characters. const add refuses other names; the generator skips them with a comment. Lowercase names are allowed (const add warns that the convention is UPPER_CASE). An empty value is exported as empty.

    Expansion. A leading ~ or ~/ becomes $HOME. Only references to named variables expand; every other character, $ included, is literal:

    Written zsh / bash fish
    $NAME expands (emitted as ${NAME}, so $HOME:h or $HOME[1] are not zsh modifiers / subscripts) expands
    ${NAME} expands expands
    ${NAME<op>...}, op = - + ? (each also with a leading :), #, %, / expands, e.g. ${X:-d}, ${X#pre}, ${X/a/b} literal
    ${#NAME} expands literal
    Any other ${...}: ${X=v} / ${X:=v} (would assign X), ${X@P}, ${X[1]}, ${X:1}, ${X: -2}, ${X^}, ${HOME:h}, ${(e)X} literal literal
    $1, $$, $?, $%, a trailing $, an unclosed ${ literal literal
    $(cmd), `cmd` literal (never run) literal
    ", \ literal literal

    The text inside an expanding ${NAME:-...} follows the same rules, so ${X:-$(cmd)} never runs cmd.

    Secret masking. An entry looks secret when its name contains (any case) KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASSWD, PASS, API, CREDENTIAL, AUTH, PRIVATE, SESSION, COOKIE, SIGNATURE, CERT or DSN, or when its value starts with a known token prefix (sk-, sk_, pk_live_, rk_live_, ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_, github_pat_, glpat-, xoxb-, xoxp-, xoxa-, xapp-, AKIA, ASIA, AIza, ya29., eyJ, npm_, hf_, -----BEGIN) or is a URL with a password (scheme://user:pass@host). Empty values are never masked.

    Where Shows
    wayu const list (text and --json, with or without --full) ******** for secret-looking constants and environment variables; --reveal shows them
    TUI constants view Masked; v toggles reveal
    Dry-run previews Masked
    wayu const get NAME The real value

    Masking only affects display: core.<ext> holds and exports the real values. Files holding constant values (entries.json, its backups, core.<ext>, path_sync.<ext>) are owner-only (0600).

    Other files you edit#

    hooks.conf#

    $WAYU_CONFIG_DIR/hooks.conf runs a command before or after a wayu operation. wayu hooks shows the configured hooks; wayu hooks edit opens the file (creating a commented example).

    # test hooks
post_constant_add = echo added {name}={value} >> ~/hook.log
pre_constant_remove = sh -c 'echo removing {name} >> ~/hook.log'
post_constant_remove = echo "gone: $WAYU_HOOK_NAME" >> ~/hook.log

    Format: one event = command per line; # starts a comment line; a pair of quotes is removed only when it wraps the whole command as one quoted string (pre_export = "echo 'Generating...'"), so "/bin/echo" {path} "done" is kept as written; unknown keys are ignored; for a repeated key the last line wins.

    Event {path} {name} {value}
    pre_path_add, post_path_add directory
    pre_path_remove, post_path_remove directory (also when removed by key)
    pre_alias_add, post_alias_add, pre_alias_remove, post_alias_remove alias name command
    pre_constant_add, post_constant_add, pre_constant_remove, post_constant_remove variable name value (empty for an encrypted secret)
    pre_plugin_install, post_plugin_install plugin name
    pre_export, post_export (around wayu export / build turbo)

    The same values are in the environment as WAYU_HOOK_PATH, WAYU_HOOK_NAME and WAYU_HOOK_VALUE (empty when not meaningful).

    Placeholder quoting:

    Written Result
    Unquoted: echo Adding {path} Replaced by "${WAYU_HOOK_PATH}": the value is one word, never parsed as code.
    Inside '...': sh -c 'echo {path}' Left as "${WAYU_HOOK_PATH}" for the inner shell, which expands it quoted.
    Inside "...", also within '...': sh -c "echo {value}", sh -c 'sh -c "echo {value}"' Refused. Any wayu operation that would run hooks exits 78 before writing anything and names the line; wayu hooks marks it INVALID. Use "$WAYU_HOOK_VALUE" when you need double quotes.

    Hooks run with sh -c, stdin on /dev/null; their exit status is ignored. In the CLI a hook's stdout and stderr are shown (in the TUI they are captured). Pre-hooks run only when the operation will change something, post-hooks only after a successful write, and none under --dry-run. Hooks run outside wayu's config lock (pre-hooks before it is taken, post-hooks after it is released), so a hook may run wayu itself. A hook still running after 30 s is killed with its child processes (the CLI prints a warning naming it); a timeout = <seconds> line in hooks.conf changes that limit (whole seconds above 0; other values keep 30).

    plugins.json#

    $WAYU_DATA_DIR/plugins.json (JSON5: comments and trailing commas allowed) is written by wayu plugin ... and may be hand-edited or synced. Plugins are cloned to $WAYU_DATA_DIR/plugins/<name>.

    After syncing this file to a new machine, run wayu plugin restore (or preview with --dry-run). It backs up the imported file, replaces installed_path with this machine's <data>/plugins/<name>, restores missing checkouts at their recorded revisions and regenerates the loaders. The version remains "1.0"; ordinary commands still reject paths outside the current plugins directory. Existing checkouts are kept, including edits; use plugin update explicitly to advance them. See cli.md.

    {
  "version": "1.0",
  "last_updated": "2026-11-07T14:35:37Z",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "zsh-autosuggestions",
      "url": "https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions.git",
      "enabled": true,
      "shell": "ZSH",
      "installed_path": "/home/me/.local/share/wayu/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions",
      "use": [],
      "template": "Source",
      "dependencies": [],
      "priority": 100,
    },
  ],
}
    Field Type Meaning
    version string "1.0".
    last_updated string Set by wayu on every write.
    plugins[].name string Required, unique: one path component, not starting with -.
    plugins[].display_name string Alternative name accepted by plugin get/enable/....
    plugins[].url string Clone URL (validated).
    plugins[].source_type enum GitHub, GitLab, Gist, Git, Remote, Local.
    plugins[].enabled boolean Only enabled plugins load.
    plugins[].shell enum ZSH, BASH, BOTH (zsh + bash), FISH, ANY (all three).
    plugins[].installed_path string Clone dir; no leading -, no control characters.
    plugins[].use array of strings Files to source, matched at the repository root: exact names or one-* globs ("*.plugin.zsh"); no / (a ../ path is refused). Set with wayu plugin add <url> --use <file-or-glob> (repeatable). Empty: auto-detect (below).
    plugins[].template enum How each file is loaded: Source (source file), Path (prepend the plugin dir to PATH), FPath (prepend to FPATH), Autoload (autoload -Uz name), Eval (eval "$(file)").
    plugins[].git object ref_type (Branch, Tag, Commit), branch, tag, commit, pinned_ref, last_checked, remote_commit. Refs are validated.
    plugins[].dependencies array of strings Plugin names loaded before this one. Must be valid plugin names; a cycle is an error. A missing or disabled dependency is noted as a comment in plugins.<ext>.
    plugins[].priority integer Load order among plugins whose dependencies are met; lower loads earlier (default 100). Ties keep file order.
    plugins[].conflicts object Written by wayu's conflict detection.

    Enum values are strings, matched case-insensitively; numbers are rejected. Unknown keys are ignored (and dropped on the next write). Any invalid value makes every command that reads plugins.json exit 78 with the plugin and field named.

    Auto-detected entry file (no use): the first that exists of <name>.plugin.<ext>, <name>.<ext>, <name>-init.<ext>, init.<ext>, plugin.<ext>, then <name>.zsh-theme (zsh) and <name>.plugin.sh, <name>.sh (zsh, bash); otherwise every top-level *.<ext> (zsh: then *.zsh-theme). fish also loads conf.d/*.fish and functions/*.fish.

    extra.<ext> and tools.<ext>#

    $WAYU_CONFIG_DIR/tools.<ext> and $WAYU_CONFIG_DIR/extra.<ext> are plain shell scripts for anything wayu.toml does not cover (wayu init creates commented templates). They are sourced on every shell start, tools first:

    • zsh/bash: from core.<ext>, after the deferred [tools] and before login-only tools and aliases.
    • fish: from init.fish, after core.fish.

    wayu config extend edits extra.<ext>; wayu config scan --fix moves inline scripts from .zshrc into it. Edits take effect in new shells without wayu build.

    config.<ext>#

    If $WAYU_CONFIG_DIR/config.<ext> exists, its content is copied into core.<ext> (after functions, before the helpers) when core is generated. Unlike extra.<ext> it is not sourced at startup: run wayu build after editing it.

    functions/#

    $WAYU_DATA_DIR/functions/ holds one file per function (wayu function add <name> writes functions/<name>.<ext>). Sourced at startup:

    Shell Sources
    zsh *.zsh only
    bash *.bash only
    fish *.fish only

    scripts/ and bin/#

    $WAYU_DATA_DIR/scripts/ holds the sources of wayu script (one NAME.<ext> per script; the directory is the list) and $WAYU_DATA_DIR/bin/ what runs: a relative symlink to the source for interpreted languages, the compiled binary plus .NAME.hash (hash of the source and build command it was built from) for swift and any source with a wayu: build = ... header (see wayu script in docs/cli.md). Use wayu script rather than editing bin/. Once bin/ holds a script, core.<ext> and path_sync.<ext> put it first among wayu's PATH entries (zsh, bash, fish), so a script may shadow a tool of the same name.

    completions/#

    $WAYU_DATA_DIR/completions/ (wayu completions add / generate write here):

    Shell Used as
    zsh Prepended to fpath (files named _<command>); compinit runs in interactive shells and rebuilds .zcompdump when the dir's file list, or any fpath dir or its mtime, changed
    bash Sources *.bash-completion and *.bash
    fish Prepended to fish_complete_path

    alias-sources.conf#

    $WAYU_CONFIG_DIR/alias-sources.conf lists external alias sources that wayu alias list shows as read-only (they are not defined in the shell):

    # dir <path> <command_template>
dir ~/.config/fabric/patterns fabric --pattern {name}

    Each entry of <path> (leading ~ expanded) becomes a name; {name} in the template is replaced with it. Lines not starting with dir and comment lines are ignored.

    Generated files#

    Do not edit these; wayu overwrites them. They are regenerated by wayu build, wayu init and every path / alias / const change (CLI or TUI), for every shell initialized in the data dir.

    File (data dir) Content
    init.<ext> Entry point your rc file sources: loads core.<ext> (prints a hint to run wayu build when it is missing). Written by wayu init. An unmodified copy of the current or previous template is replaced when the template changes (backup first); an edited one is kept, with a warning.
    core.<ext> Everything init.<ext> loads, precomputed from wayu.toml and entries.json (zsh also core.zsh.zwc, compiled in the background).
    path_sync.<ext> The PATH entry list (after bin/ when it holds a script); line 1 is its signature. The prompt hook re-sources it when the signature changes.
    turbo.<ext> zsh/bash. Same content as core.<ext>, refreshed with it, only if it exists (created by wayu export).
    plugins.<ext> Plugin loader, regenerated on any plugin change and by wayu init.
    plugins/config.zsh [settings] autosuggestions_accept_keys bindings.
    secrets.json Encrypted constants (see [secrets]); written by wayu const add --secret, const rm, secrets rekey and the multi-machine secrets recipient / recovery commands (experimental). Not generated from wayu.toml.
    backup/ Timestamped backups <file>.backup.YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.UUUUUU[-N] (UTC), 5 newest per file (see wayu backup). <file> is the name of a file directly in the config/data dir, @ + its relative path with / as % for a nested one (@functions%init.zsh), or the path of a file outside them (.zshrc, .config%zsh%.zshrc). Files named otherwise are ignored.

    Also $WAYU_DATA_DIR/.wayu.lock (lock shared by concurrent wayu commands) and the evalcache under ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/wayu/evalcache.

    Load order#

    core.zsh / core.bash, each # === ... === line a section:

    1. WAYU_CONFIG_DIR / WAYU_DATA_DIR exports (only when not default)
    2. Constants
    3. Secrets (session cache; only when secrets.json holds values)
    4. bin/ (scripts) and PATH entries (and the live PATH sync hook)
    5. Completions (zsh: fpath; compinit and the compinit guard in interactive shells, see [settings])
    6. functions/
    7. config.<ext> content
    8. Helpers (evalcache; zsh: zsh-defer in interactive shells, wayu_compile)
    9. Eager [tools]
    10. Native prompt (zsh, interactive, [prompt] enabled = true)
    11. Plugins (plugins.<ext>; zsh: plugins/config.zsh, interactive shells only, after the first prompt with defer_plugins; zsh with [settings] autosuggest / highlight: the built-in suggestions and syntax highlighting first)
    12. Deferred [tools]
    13. tools.<ext>
    14. extra.<ext>
    15. Login-only [tools]
    16. Aliases

    core.fish: directory exports, constants, secrets, PATH entries, completions, functions/*.fish, config.fish content, evalcache helper, eager [tools], the native prompt ([prompt] enabled = true), plugins.fish, deferred [tools], login-only [tools], aliases. init.fish then sources tools.fish and extra.fish; turbo.fish (wayu export) is core.fish followed by those two.
